title: Canal Street jitney dance halls
summary: Father played jitney or taxi dances on Canal Street; Harold recalls his own band at the job he got from James Davis, and playing with P. Roy and Walter P. Sean.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: When y'all was living on some foot, do you remember what, the job he was playing? He was playing one of those taxi dances.
He used to play on Canal Street. Yeah. Canal between Villery and.
And he'd go out to the Jump Hotel on that side of the bank.
Uh huh. Jitney dancing. Do you remember what that was, Darryl?

I forgot, I forgot the name of the place, but I had my band in there once. In fact, it was my band and it was James Davis's job and he took my band in there. And after he got on his feet, you know, I'm out. You know how that goes.
Do you remember that place Shakey or another?

It wasn't the Hummer Boogie. No, the Hummer Boogie was in the district. This was on Canal on that side. How old is it? It was just like, you know, like if you would walk in an apartment house, that's the way that you're walking at it. It was a big dance hall. Oh, yes. A big beautiful stage and everything. Yeah. You know, Jitney's Jitney dance. A Jitney dance.
Yeah. And paid 10 cents a day.

The music box was on Canal. And Carondelet. Yeah. Right where Stein's Clown's story. Because I played the Crescent Billion Hall across the street a couple of nights with P. Roy and I played there with Walter P. Sean. My daddy used to play with P. Roy. Yeah.
